narration: In the initializing process, a pre-trained 3D Gaussian Splatting model with frozen parameters undergoes Frequency Guided Densification.
In Phase 1 of densification, the rendering quality contribution of each Gaussian is evaluated, and unneeded Gaussians are pruned and removed.
In Phase 2, multi-view patches are transformed via Discrete Fourier Transform with a quadratic mask to detect high frequencies and split Gaussians in detailed areas.
After densification, the resulting 3D Gaussian model is frozen, and its parameters are used to construct gradient masks for position, color, opacity, rotation, and scale.
During the fine-tuning process, the watermarked Gaussian model is unfrozen and differentiable rendering generates 2D scene views.
The rendered view is decomposed by Discrete Wavelet Transform, sending low frequencies to a pre-trained decoder to extract the embedded watermark and compute message loss L_m.
High-frequency wavelet components are regularized by loss L_w against the ground truth, alongside spatial reconstruction and perceptual LPIPS losses.
All losses are combined into total loss L_total, driving the optimizer via a Hadamard product with the gradient mask to selectively update the watermarked Gaussians.
